Team — forwarding Ben's note and the customer's proposed parity language. Short summary: Nomos (strategic HS account) is asking for a broad parity / benchmarking right that would allow them to compare prices for any "materially similar" product and request rebates/credits if they find a better price elsewhere. They also want audit access for pricing records.

Why this matters: those two items (broad parity + audit) create an open-ended economic liability and could cascade across our commercial plays in the healthcare vertical. Nomos represents ~2.4M ARR in year 1 and is a reference customer; there's strategic value in making a concession, but we need to limit exposure.

Proposed commercial compromise for exec sign-off: 
- Approve 12% list discount for first 12 months (as proposed).
- Accept a parity clause but narrow it to: (i) same product SKU/edition; (ii) US-only; (iii) 12-month timebox from signing; (iv) customer audit limited to once per 12 months, for a narrowly defined data set (invoiced list prices and discounted rates), conducted under NDA and at Nomos' expense.
- Add a cap on cumulative credits tied to parity disputes at 10% of first-year ARR.

Ask: Laura, can you confirm legal can produce a clean redline that implements the above constraints and that the audit mechanics are defensible? Monica, finance needs to confirm the cap and the $ figure for the credit reserve. Rishi, I need a one-line approval (or alternate instruction) to give Ben the green light to accept these constraints with the customer.

Attaching Ben's redline and a quick markup I made (Nomos_redline_term_sheet.pdf).

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Nomos term sheet + market access / parity language — legal review and recommended carve-ins

Dylan / team — reviewed the customer's markup and Ben's note. High level: the language as drafted is problematic because it is open-ended and hooks into "materially similar" without objective gates. Key legal risks: unlimited lookback claims, broad audit scope that could implicate customer data requests, and a vague remedy (rebate/credit) that isn't capped.

Recommended legal redlines (summary):
- Replace "market parity" with "List Price Parity for Substantially Similar Offerings": define "substantially similar" by explicit SKU/feature matrix we both agree to in an appendix.
- Limit geography: US-only.
- Timebox parity to 12 months from Effective Date.
- Audit: Nomos can request one audit per 12 months; scope is limited to (a) Redwood's publicly listed list prices and (b) customer-specific executed pricing for materially similar SKUs; audits to be conducted by an agreed third-party auditor under mutual NDA; costs borne by Nomos unless audit reveals breach >5% in which case Redwood pays for that audit.
- Remedy cap: limit cumulative credits to 10% of year-1 ARR (as Dylan proposed) and require that any credits be applied prospectively on renewal/or as a one-time invoice credit tied to a confirmed breach.
- Add salvage language: if the customer insists on broader audit or global parity, require explicit exec waiver and proportional economic quid (e.g., increased discount or guaranteed minimum term).

I attached a marked-up clause (parity_clause_markup.docx) with redlines and a proposed appendix template for SKU mapping. If you want, I can convert the appendix into a short exhibit that we can pre-fill with Nomos' SKU list and our mapping.

Risk assessment: with the proposed redlines the business risk is manageable — the customer gets some parity visibility but we avoid open-ended liabilities. Without those limits, we risk both economic and operational overhead (frequent audits, benchmarking disputes).

Next steps: 
- Dylan/Ben: get confirmation from Nomos whether they will accept SKU-limited parity + 12-month timebox.
- Monica/Finance: confirm that the 10% cap on credits is acceptable and we can reserve a $75k one-time credit if needed (numbers below).
- If all good, Rishi: please provide one-line approval for this commercial posture so I can send the clean redline back.

Laura Bennett
